newsitem.title: CANADA: W Canada wheat, barley output above avg - CWB's Hehn.
newsitem.headline: W Canada wheat, barley output above avg - CWB's Hehn.

text.p: Western Canadian spring wheat, durum wheat and barley production in crop year 1996/97 (Aug/July) was expected to exceed the five-year average output, the chief commissioner of the Canadian Wheat Board told Reuters.
"We're expecting a production of about 23 million tonnes of spring wheat and our five-year average is 22 million," CWB chief commissioner Lorne Hehn said.
The biggest spring wheat crop, Canada Western Red Spring wheat, was forecast to produce 19.6 million tonnes compared with the five year average of 19.0 million tonnes, Hehn said.
Durum wheat output was forecast at 4.36 million tonnes compared with the 4.10 million tonne average over the last five years, Hehn said.
Barley production was expected to come in at 15.0 million tonnes across the Prairie provinces, he said.
Statistics Canada on Monday forecast spring wheat output for all of Canada at 24.297 million tonnes, durum output at 4.36 million tonnes and barley at 16.26 million tonnes.
